updater_competence.reason: Adaptive stopping phenomenon exists, but the updater stream has only 19.4% nonzero target-effect rounds, below the 25% prerequisite.
updater_competence.scientific_role: hard prerequisite before Gate 1; failure blocks controller fitting without rejecting the stopping phenomenon

entries.basis: Keep the competent ALFWorld interaction horizon at 50 steps.
Twenty-four fit sequences and twenty-four hidden sequences provide a confirmatory controller split while preserving frozen hidden evaluation.
Four update rounds expose early/late stopping and over-update harm without unbounded search.
At least one quarter of hidden sequences must contain a successful candidate round before call-saving can be scientifically identified.
A 25% call reduction at matched utility is the preregistered minimum effect worth a formal P0 claim.
Twenty-four hidden sequences have 1/24 = 4.17pp binary success resolution; a 5pp tolerance is observable whereas 2pp is not.
Qualified Qwen react-family throughput predicts about 7.45 worst-case GPU-hours; cap includes a safety margin.

identifiability.true_false_question: Do the frozen sequences contain target variation and policy disagreement that can identify a call-saving controller?

throughput.reference: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct react-family on server 60 RTX3090, 24 ID environments, 50-step cap

recovery.restart_policy: Preserve complete sequence artifacts for diagnosis; restart a fresh confirmatory run under the same frozen contract after any runtime stop.
recovery.partial_artifact_policy: Partial sequences never enter the Pilot Registry or formal controller comparison.

scope_conditions: update stream has nonzero target effects

assumptions.statement: Different update rounds create enough outcome variation to make stopping identifiable.
assumptions.observable_check: nonzero effect fraction plus early-stop/late-stop/rollback-or-harm archetypes

assumptions.statement: Observable local state contains information about the marginal value and risk of another update.

principle_certificate.mechanism: When update value diminishes or regression risk rises, an adaptive controller can stop before unnecessary or harmful updates and preserve useful earlier changes.

predictions.statement: Frozen update sequences contain distinct optimal stopping points and nontrivial future-benefit variation.
predictions.observable: stop/continue/rollback target entropy and oracle headroom

predictions.statement: Given qualified sequences, state-dependent stopping saves update calls at matched success versus the strongest fixed/simple stopping rule.
predictions.observable: held-out call saving at bounded success loss plus policy disagreement

operationalization.validity_check: same sequence access and matched-information baselines

falsification.contradiction_rule: Reject only the state-dependent stopping sub-principle after a qualified nondegenerate update stream and valid controller target fail the preregistered matched hidden test.

failure_update_rules.design-nonidentifiable: repair sequence construction/target variation; no principle negative
failure_update_rules.assumption-violation: revise scope/assumption and derive a new prediction
failure_update_rules.matched-simplification: weaken/merge the learned-controller realization, not the adaptive-stopping phenomenon
